clinical_category: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control

semantic_correction.stem: An asymptomatic healthcare worker has an occupational measles exposure. The worker had no MMR dose before the exposure and has no other presumptive evidence of measles immunity. Which work restriction follows current CDC guidance?

options.A: Exclude from work from day 5 after the first exposure through day 21 after the last exposure.
options.B: Allow unrestricted work after postexposure prophylaxis as long as the worker remains asymptomatic.
options.C: Exclude from work only if fever, cough, conjunctivitis, or a measles-compatible rash develops.
options.D: Exclude from work for the first 4 days after exposure, then return with routine symptom monitoring.

semantic_correction.rationale: CDC's December 10, 2025 healthcare-personnel infection-control guideline recommends postexposure prophylaxis for asymptomatic healthcare personnel without presumptive evidence of measles immunity and exclusion from work from the 5th day after the first exposure through the 21st day after the last exposure, regardless of receipt of postexposure prophylaxis. CDC separately states that work restriction is not necessary for an exposed worker who had already received a first MMR dose before exposure; the stem explicitly excludes that exception. Therefore, option A is the uniquely applicable restriction.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: For measles-exposed healthcare personnel without presumptive immunity and without a pre-exposure first MMR dose, apply CDC work exclusion from day 5 after first exposure through day 21 after last exposure.
semantic_correction.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)

semantic_correction.source_claim_supported: CDC recommends work exclusion from day 5 after first measles exposure through day 21 after last exposure for asymptomatic HCP without presumptive immunity, regardless of PEP, while providing a no-work-restriction exception for HCP who had received a first MMR dose before exposure.

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup: corrected a clinically important ambiguity by explicitly excluding CDC's pre-exposure first-MMR-dose exception; refreshed the source to the December 10, 2025 CDC HCP guideline and rebuilt the distractors as parallel work-restriction plans.

audit_findings_append.source_locator: 2025 HCP guideline, Measles Recommendations item 2, printed p. 23/PDF p. 23
audit_findings_append.blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control, printed pp. 24 and 26
audit_findings_append.finding: The original stem said only 'without presumptive evidence of immunity,' which could include an exposed worker who had received one MMR dose before exposure; CDC explicitly exempts that subgroup from work restriction. The revised stem removes the second-answer risk by specifying no pre-exposure MMR dose.

option_audit.A: Correct. It states the exact CDC work-exclusion interval for the susceptible exposed worker defined in the stem.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. CDC specifies the exclusion interval regardless of receipt of postexposure prophylaxis for this subgroup.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. Waiting for symptoms would miss the CDC pre-symptomatic work-restriction period for a susceptible exposed worker.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. CDC does not use a 4-day postexposure exclusion interval for this circumstance.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. The stem explicitly excludes the CDC first-dose-before-exposure exception, leaving A as the sole applicable work-restriction plan.
cueing_check: All four options are work-restriction plans of comparable length and specificity; no absolute-word or unique-length cue identifies A.

checks: December 10, 2025 CDC HCP guideline freshly verified
day-5-after-first through day-21-after-last interval verified directly
stem rewritten to exclude exception and second-answer risk
